brief.scenario: Mr Jones, 68, has had worsening right groin pain on walking for a year.
brief.task: Examine his right hip. You will be stopped at 6 minutes to present your findings and answer questions.

beforeYouWalkIn.frame: Gait first, then look, feel, measure, move, and the Thomas test.
beforeYouWalkIn.trap: Getting the Trendelenburg side wrong: the pelvis drops on the side of the lifted leg.
beforeYouWalkIn.firstMove: "Could I watch you walk to the end of the room and back?"

grid.label: Preparation
grid.fail: Starts moving the hip without asking about pain.
grid.pass: Introduces, confirms identity, explains, gains consent, asks about pain, cleans hands, exposes to shorts.
grid.high: Watches his face for pain throughout and moves the hip only within comfort.

grid.label: Gait and Trendelenburg
grid.fail: Omits gait, or gets the Trendelenburg interpretation backwards.
grid.borderline: Performs the test correctly but can't say which side is abnormal.
grid.pass: Observes gait; performs the Trendelenburg test standing on each leg.
grid.high: Explains a positive test: standing on the right, the left side of the pelvis drops, meaning weak right abductors.

grid.label: Look and feel
grid.pass: Inspects for scars, wasting and deformity; palpates the greater trochanter for tenderness.
grid.high: Compares with the other side, and palpates the lumbar spine and sacroiliac joints.

grid.label: Leg lengths
grid.pass: True length: ASIS to medial malleolus. Apparent length: umbilicus to medial malleolus.
grid.high: Squares the pelvis first, and explains apparent shortening from fixed adduction or tilt.

grid.label: Movement and Thomas test
grid.fail: Moves the hip without stabilising the pelvis.
grid.pass: Flexion, abduction, adduction, internal and external rotation; Thomas test for fixed flexion deformity.
grid.high: Feels the lumbar lordosis flatten during the Thomas test, and notes internal rotation is often lost first in osteoarthritis.

grid.label: Completing the examination
grid.pass: Says they would examine the lumbar spine and knee, and check distal neurovascular status.
grid.high: Explains why: hip pain can be referred to the knee, and spinal pathology can mimic hip pain.

grid.label: Presentation at the signal
grid.pass: Summarises the positive findings and gives a most likely diagnosis.
grid.high: Leads with the key findings, states the important negatives, and commits.

grid.label: Diagnosis and referral
grid.fail: Insists on an X-ray before any diagnosis, or uses age alone to refuse surgery.
grid.pass: Diagnoses osteoarthritis clinically at 45 or over with activity-related pain and morning stiffness of 30 minutes or less.
grid.high: Refers for joint replacement on symptoms and failed non-surgical care, not scores, age or BMI.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: [Asks him to lie down and starts rotating the hip without asking about pain.]

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: [Measures leg lengths with the pelvis tilted.]

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: I moved his hip and it hurt.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: How would you confirm the diagnosis?

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: He needs an MRI before I can say.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Hello, I'm Dr Patel. Can I confirm your name and date of birth? I'd like to examine your right hip. Where does it hurt? [Consent; cleans hands; exposes to shorts.]

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Could you walk to the end of the room and back? … Now stand on your right leg, holding my hands, and lift the left. [Then the other side.]

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: [Inspects front, side and back; palpates the greater trochanter.]

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: [Measures ASIS to medial malleolus, then umbilicus to medial malleolus, both sides.]

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: [Tests each movement.] Now I'll bend your left hip right up. [Thomas test.]

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: I'd also examine the lumbar spine and knee and check the pulses and sensation. Thank you. [Cleans hands.]

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Mr Jones has an antalgic gait, a positive Trendelenburg test on the right, 2 cm apparent shortening on the right, a fixed flexion deformity on the Thomas test, and painful restriction of internal rotation. This is most likely right hip osteoarthritis.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: It can be diagnosed clinically: he's over 45 with activity-related pain and short morning stiffness.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Hello, I'm Dr Patel. Can I confirm your name and date of birth? I'd like to watch you walk and then examine your right hip. Tell me straight away if anything hurts. [Cleans hands; exposes to shorts; watches his face.]

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: [Antalgic gait.] Stand on your right leg and lift the left… the left side of your pelvis drops, so your right hip abductors are weak.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: [Inspects all sides; palpates trochanter, lumbar spine, sacroiliac joints; compares with the left.]

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: [Squares the pelvis.] True lengths are equal; the right is apparently shorter, which suggests fixed adduction.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: [Movements; hand under the lumbar spine during the Thomas test until the lordosis flattens.] Internal rotation is the most restricted.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: I'd complete this with the spine and knee, because hip pain is often felt in the knee, and check distal neurovascular status. Thank you. [Cleans hands.]

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Right hip: antalgic gait, positive Trendelenburg, apparent but not true shortening, a fixed flexion deformity, and restricted, painful internal rotation. No scars and no spinal tenderness. This is right hip osteoarthritis.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: It's a clinical diagnosis. If his symptoms substantially affect his quality of life and non-surgical treatment hasn't worked, I'd refer for hip replacement, based on clinical assessment, not scores, age or BMI.

failures.consequence: Misses scars from previous surgery and trochanteric tenderness.
Misses referred pain from the spine and knee.
Can't separate true shortening at the hip from pelvic tilt.

recovery.line: Let me restate: standing on the right, the left side dropped, so the right abductors are weak.
Before I finish, I'd like to check for a fixed flexion deformity with the Thomas test.

knowledge.fact: Positive Trendelenburg: the pelvis drops on the side of the lifted leg; the abductors of the standing leg are weak.
True length: ASIS to medial malleolus. Apparent length: umbilicus to medial malleolus.
Diagnose osteoarthritis clinically, without imaging, at 45 or over with activity-related pain and morning stiffness of 30 minutes or less.
Refer for joint replacement using clinical assessment, not scoring systems; do not exclude on age, smoking, comorbidity or BMI.

recall.think: Gait, then look, feel, measure, move.
recall.say: "Could I watch you walk to the end of the room and back?"
do: Thomas test with a hand under the spine

numbers.meaning: clinical OA diagnosis with activity-related pain

recall.finish: Clinical diagnosis; refer on symptoms, not scores.

partner.opening: Please examine this patient's right hip. I'll stop you at 6 minutes.
partner.actorBrief: You are Mr Jones, 68. Right groin pain when walking, worse at the end of the day, stiffness for about 15 minutes in the morning. It hurts when your hip is turned inwards.

reveals.finding: Antalgic gait, shorter stance on the right.

reveals.trigger: Trendelenburg test, standing on the right
reveals.finding: The left side of the pelvis drops.
True lengths equal; right apparently 2 cm shorter.
Right thigh lifts off the couch as the lordosis flattens: fixed flexion deformity.
Internal rotation markedly restricted and painful.
Say: "Please stop there and present your findings."

push.question: What does a positive Trendelenburg test mean?
push.expect: Weak abductors on the standing side.

push.question: How do you tell true from apparent shortening?
push.expect: Square the pelvis; ASIS versus umbilicus to medial malleolus.

push.question: Does he need an X-ray to diagnose osteoarthritis?
push.expect: No, it can be diagnosed clinically.

curveballs.prompt: His BMI is 38. Should he be refused referral?
curveballs.safeAnswer: No: BMI alone should not exclude referral for joint replacement.

curveballs.prompt: His pain is mainly in the knee.
curveballs.safeAnswer: Hip pain is often referred to the knee: examine both.
